engagement_background.objective: Reduce total supplier costs by securing $0.7–$1.4 million in annual savings across key spend categories and to put basic procurement processes and controls in place, thereby increasing Advantia Health’s enterprise value for its investors.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya will run strategic sourcing and/or incumbent-negotiation events for 10 spend categories representing about $19 million of the $45 million total AP/P-card spend (e.g., employee benefits, IUDs, diagnostic devices, billing/RCM, medical supplies).  Work also includes a light procurement-process / controls review.  Some categories may later be excluded if detailed data prove un-addressable; employee benefits is an optional work-stream.
constraints_challenges: Supplier fragmentation and multiple small purchases limit leverage across several categories.
Limited strategic procurement resources and focus inside Advantia prior to the project.
Separate AP and P-card systems for the Mid-Atlantic and Heartland business units create data integration challenges.
Line-item usage data are incomplete; some high-spend suppliers may not provide detailed history despite repeated requests.
Need to avoid parallel buying actions by Advantia during the project to prevent market confusion, per the services agreement.
Realization of certain savings requires behavior changes at clinic level (e.g., ordering IUDs in lots of five, switching distributors).

procurement_environment.data_availability: 12-month AP data and YTD P-card data were obtainable, but item-level details and contracts are scattered across vendors and two ERP/payment systems (Advantia and Heartland).
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple supplier name variations, limited GL/item descriptions, no unified contract repository, and gaps where suppliers withheld usage files.
